title: CI had not run for 46 days: two stacked breakages, the second hiding the first
detail: Verified by the controller over all 554 runs: 529 failure, 23 success, last success 2026-07-22T22:53:02Z. Green on run 34053229048 with all six corpus guards naming themselves (6 verified, 0 skipped) and 2647 tests passed.

title: A second video-port write in one instruction re-charges the first write's stall, 40 percent over-billed
detail: now_mclk is set once per instruction while fifo_slot_clock is absolute. Six stalling writes charge 967 cycles against a true 281. data_read_at does it correctly one function away. Every existing test stops at the fifth write.

title: The Z80 reset line is a hold, not a reset: a halted sound driver never restarts
detail: Measured with two controls. Z80 exposes no reset method; the core is constructed once and never re-initialised. The rule was written into docs/2026-07-22-sound-stack-recon.md:224 in July with 'pin it, do not let it drift' and never implemented.

title: About 560 real Z80 encodings panic uncontained; one byte in a guest driver kills the process
detail: Measured by executing every prefixed encoding under catch_unwind: ED 20, DD 46, FD 46, DDCB 224, FDCB 224. No catch_unwind anywhere in production. A commercial ROM reached this class before.

title: Every replay frame renders a full attributed scanline and discards it, to produce three status bits
detail: wants_scanlines defaults to false and oracle-replay's Fanout overrides neither. The tool whose pitch is one playthrough instead of many pays a discarded raster every frame.

title: Three guard tests and the guards they test both vanish under --release
detail: Controller re-measured: 11 tests in debug, 8 in release. They do not report as ignored; the count drops silently.

title: A reset could strand or roll back the owner's battery save
detail: Not hosted-only, so the booked mitigation did not cover it. The existing guard asserted on the machine and never the file, and its helper never ran the debounce. Fixed structurally in Bus::call_stamped; two new rows read the real .srm and each goes red naming the file.

title: The request side of the wire has a machine-readable contract and no differential against it
detail: 57 integer bounds in the fragments; jsonschema is a dev-dependency only; every bound re-implemented by hand in 62 handlers. 21 of 62 methods have no negative-value test. One Engine on one thread with no catch_unwind.

title: The listing-freshness guard is blind to two of the three populations it gates
detail: Compares address rows only; equates and phase are disjoint populations, and lookup_equate attaches this very caveat. Change an equate's value and the server answers the old number quietly. Zero equate coverage in the freshness suite.

title: The most-repeated safety claim in the tree names a mechanism that does not exist
detail: Repeated in eight source comments, two escalating to 'none may ever be added'. No compile-fail harness exists in the workspace and no test asserts the signature. A correct example naming a real mechanism sits 4000 lines away in the same crate.

title: The drift gate landed this morning covers none of the eleven symbols the panel landed this afternoon needs
detail: Controller re-measured: 25 rows, zero matching Parallax|Raster|BgAnim, against a working control. Controller correction: the FIXTURES are the stale side, not the panel.

title: A per-line scroll value is fetched once per pixel, 320 times more often than it can change
detail: plane_hscroll takes no x and does two VRAM reads. The line-hoisted copy already sits in ASlotCtx three lines away. Confirmed in the shipped binary by objdump.

title: A damaged-but-binding symbol file is disclosed on three surfaces and silent on the two that answer programs
detail: Load a truncated listing in the window and you get a warning; load the same file over the socket and it is accepted silently. Names then resolve to a plausible, healthy-looking, wrong routine.

title: The completed-frame reader exists four times and only the copy scheduled for deletion is tested
detail: The retirement deletes the only tested copy and leaves two untested, one of which backs emulator/screenshot and every hosted client.

title: A doc says callers must not reach this arm and the sole caller does
detail: Space::Z80 is a live selector entry. The covering test picks Space::Vram and asserts a message the Z80 path fails.

title: The I/O decode rule is applied on the read path and contradicted on the write path
detail: Read cites its evidence; write states the opposite rule citing nothing. Word writes are unaffected, which is why no golden catches it. The seat reported the contradiction and refused to adjudicate the hardware question.

title: A bounded list bypasses the blessed helper its sibling uses on the identical bound
detail: No total, no returned, no limit, where the helper's own doc makes all three the rule and the schema makes them required. The fragment was transcribed to the hand-rolled shape, so conformance is structurally blind.

title: Nothing in the sweep was exercised against a running emulator, window, or full suite
detail: Charter rules 2 to 4, with the owner's window live throughout. Every runtime-dependent claim is tagged rather than asserted.

title: The 20-agent cap degraded three seats that ran, not only the five it delayed
detail: A2, ERR and P2 each had helper agents refused and pattern-swept engine.rs and ui.rs rather than reading them. All three disclosed it unprompted. Coverage is narrower than 22 seats implies.

title: F-THREE-MASKED-RENDERERS is not a live drift risk: both divergences are unreachable
detail: The three copies differ in two guards, but both depend on a short or empty row and resolve_line_masked sets width unconditionally, including on the display-disabled early return. Dead code. What survives is the missing assertion.

title: The audio-repair door-that-runs-no-repair lead is refuted
detail: Every machine-replacing door runs it, structurally, in both windows. The bus-notification half of the same lead was confirmed and is a separate finding.

title: land.sh G1 is not the only thing between a fresh worktree and a false green
detail: G1 only counts files; the real backstop is six in-suite refusals armed by CI=1 that check named manifests. Residual: a human typing the raw cargo command gets CI unset and every corpus row skips invisibly.

title: PIN.tsv is not restated anywhere in code
detail: No sha, byte count or freeze revision from the pin is hardcoded in Rust or tools. The pin is read, never restated.

title: 576 test functions added over 250 commits, 11 removed, zero silent deletions
detail: Six were renamed because the behaviour changed. No guard was deleted and left claimed as live in code.

title: Layer and LayerMask cannot gain a variant without declaring it everywhere
detail: ALL is test-guarded, every match exhaustive with no catch-all, and targets() derives the wire names with a test pinning the derivation against the vendored fragment in both directions.

title: DIMENSIONS.tsv is derived and re-verified every run, not transcribed
detail: Re-measured through SymbolTable against independently pinned bytes, with a positive control that panics on an uncovered probe kind.

title: Symbol resolution is a binary search over a pre-sorted index and the Arc clones are refcount bumps
detail: Expected to find a linear scan and did not.

title: The SAT cache's two-copies-of-one-truth is correct by design
detail: The staleness being modelled is the hardware's own, so recomputation would be the wrong answer. Documented with its reason and guarded by a test.

title: Around twenty idiom candidates checked and cleared as deliberate, each with its reason in place
detail: Includes a hand-formatted address whose sum can exceed u32 and five of six debug asserts carrying a stated reason, one naming the test that would actually catch it.

title: The Z80 reset line is a hold, not a reset: a halted sound driver never restarts
detail: Fixed. Z80::reset clears PC, I, R, IFF1, IFF2, IM and halted, and preserves the register file, index registers and SP; fires on the asserting edge only. Eleven mutations, each red on the row under test, including the silent-forever case. End-to-end test drives the real bus and observes EXECUTION, not a register or a latch. singlestep_z80 708,000 cases, 0 failures. The deferral that licensed this stated its own expiry condition in July and nobody returned; that doc now carries the pin.

title: The drift gate landed this morning covers none of the eleven symbols the panel landed this afternoon needs
detail: Fixed. Manifest 25 rows to 85; the control that read 0 now reads 65. Twelve dimensions pinned across four listings, including three pinned as ABSENT so a symbol becoming present also reddens. Gate deliberately left GREEN: the agent argued, correctly, that writing the engine's current addresses into a column the manifest binds to the frozen bytes would convert a recovery gate into a permanently-red currency gate and force the open owner decision rather than leave it open.

title: About 560 real Z80 encodings panic uncontained; one byte in a guest driver kills the emulator
detail: Closed by SERVING all 560, not by containing them. Stage 1 made refusal structural (a fault latch checked ahead of interrupt acceptance and the HALT idle; deliberately NOT halted=true, which is architectural state an interrupt would wake, vectoring into the program the core just refused). Stage 2 implemented every class graded against the vendored SingleStepTests corpus at pin ebe1875d: ED mirrors 20/20, IXH/IXL 92/92, DDCB/FDCB register-copy 448/448, 1000 cases per encoding, green on the first run; whole z80 suite 1268 files / 1,268,000 cases. New gate crates/oracle-core/tests/z80_guest_bytes_never_panic.rs steps all 1524 complete encodings plus 4096 two-prefix chains under catch_unwind: 0 panicked, 1524 executed, 0 refused. The deferral's stated reason was itself the defect: the in-tree comment said a documented-mode corpus never fetches them, true of our FILES list and false of the corpus, where all 560 answer keys existed at the pinned SHA (560 HEAD probes, 404 detector control). Controller verified with a mutation in a class the agent did not touch: forcing LD IXL,n to write IXH reddens the corpus run naming IX [DD 2E 0000] while unprefixed 2e.json still passes 1000/1000. Manifest checked as a set: 560 added, 0 of 708 removed; 1268/1268 sha256 OK. Landed GREEN 80/80 legs. Residual: Z80::refuse now has zero callers because exhaustive matches serve everything, kept deliberately with the reason at the definition. TAGGED, needs foreground: a real driver using IXH/IXL playing audibly; and a CR for a typed z80Fault key, since today it is a conditional caveat and the contract forbids parsing caveats.

title: Three guard tests and the guards they test both vanish under --release
detail: debug_assert! guards promoted to assert! in the fixture builder, plus three sibling guards of the same class in the same file. Controller measured both profiles independently, before and after: testrom:: scope was 11 tests in debug and 8 in release (dropping silently, not reporting as ignored), and is 11/11 after. oracle-core 1129 passed 0 failed in BOTH profiles. No pin was added and none is possible: once the guard is a plain assert! the profile split does not exist, and the three de-gated #[should_panic] rows ARE the regression guard, so fix and guard are one edit. Proven by demoting a guard back to debug_assert!, which reddens two rows under --release rather than deleting them (9 passed 2 failed = 11). Swept: no #[cfg(debug_assertions)] remains on any test row in crates/.

title: schema_conformance.rs's loud refusal is silent: libtest eats the SKIPPED banner
detail: ADDED TO THE LEDGER AS FIXED: this packet HIGH had no ledger row while it was open, so it never appeared in an open tally. Recorded now so the fixed record is true; it does not change any open count. The house fd-2 helper from c301f89 applied to the file that c301f89's own follower (mcp_tool_sweep.rs) names as its exemplar, which the original sweep had missed. Controller verified both directions firsthand: on main a plain cargo test prints nothing at all; at the fix the same command prints the 13-line SKIPPED banner. Worse than elsewhere because no runner sets $AETHER_CONTRACT_SCHEMA or $AETHER_CONTRACT_REPO, so the skip branch is the one every landing takes. Residual, NOT closed by this: nothing has still ever confirmed the pinned contract revision exists upstream. H5 made the refusal audible; it did not make the confirmation happen.

title: Two of four machine-replacing doors in oracle-frontend tell the bus nothing
The symbol-file acceptance policy is written out FOUR times; three survive retirement
land.sh is the third place the suite runs and does not name the aeon pin
detail: Landed as "M1: land.sh is the third place the suite runs, and it named no pin"; merged at cbacfd8.

title: Event fragments are printed, never pinned
The contract-vector runner has no floor
detail: Landed as "M3: the contract-vector runner had no floor"; merged at cbacfd8. The fix corrects the packet: the survivable drop is 170 of 176, not 175.

title: replay_playthroughs.sh discards the pin gate's verdict
detail: Landed as "M4: the one job that says this green is about THESE bytes exited 0 on a red pin"; merged at cbacfd8.

title: export_state_hash is blind to a live chip
EngineConfig limits and the schema's constants are two copies of one number
oracle-aether has become the player's model layer, not only its control surface
oracle-panels-spike is dead, with evidence
Eight zero-assertion decode tests with names promising classification they never check
detail: Landed as "decode: eight zero-assertion rows get the assertions their names promise (M9)"; merged at 47772bf. A defect in the fix itself was corrected at 5c4ee1f.

title: The safety-valve test is fed the constant the valve checks
detail: Landed as "audio/pacing: pin the constant the safety-valve tests are fed (M10)"; merged at 47772bf.

Worse than elsewhere because no runner sets $AETHER_CONTRACT_SCHEMA or $AETHER_CONTRACT_REPO, so the skip branch is the one every landing takes. Residual, NOT closed by this: nothing has still ever confirmed the pinned contract revision exists upstream. H5 made the refusal audible; it did not make the confirmation happen.

title: A second video-port write in one instruction re-charges the first write's stall, 40 percent over-billed
detail: Fixed. Both port paths measure their wait from fifo_slot_clock.max(now), which IS the already-charged mark, so no new state and no snapshot/export layout change. Landed as two commits per d-43 option 2: fix+tests, then the re-pin alone. Measured over-bill on a 10-write burst is 3.4x, not the ~40% booked; and it is rare -- 11 qualifying writes over 120 hashed frames, ~177 cycles of 143,000. One artifact moved (color_1536), same value in both harnesses, and the gradient was measured intact either side at 1407 colours before a guard was added for it.

title: The listing-freshness guard is blind to two of the three populations it gates
detail: Fixed. SymbolTable::resolves_identically compares all three populations (syms, equates, phase) and lives on the type that owns them, so a fourth population is a change in the file that gained it. Reproduced first: an equate-only rebuild returned the OLD value with no caveat and a quiet status. Two mutations, each shown applied on disk, each red.

title: The completed-frame reader exists four times and only the copy scheduled for deletion is tested
detail: Fixed by unification, not by a comment: one ScanlineCapture::completed_frame under all four consumers, each keeping only its own packing loop. The coupling is now asserted -- one mutation to the shared width rule turns all four consumers red at once. A height of 0 refuses rather than panicking now that it is a public parameter.

title: A doc says callers must not reach this arm and the sole caller does
detail: Fixed structurally rather than with a runtime check: a four-variant ReadSpace whose wire() is total, reachable only via Space::as_read_space(), which is None for Z80, so the call the doc forbade is now unrepresentable. The covering test walks Space::ALL asserting which KIND of refusal each space owes, catching drift in both directions.

title: A bounded list bypasses the blessed helper its sibling uses on the identical bound
detail: NOT A DEFECT, adjudicated upstream as CR-T / protocol.md section 11.43 at empyrean 90fc5c4 (verified here: ancestor of their origin/main, a contract commit carrying protocol.md +74, and only prose moved -- no schema and no vectors, so no re-vendor is owed). The finding's premise did not survive checking: section 3's method table already specifies this reply AS query/matches[]/truncated, adjudicated as CR-M / section 11.36, so $defs/boundedList is a definition available for reuse rather than a rule every bounded reply obeys, and our fragment agrees with the contract's prose rather than only with our code. The companion claim that our conformance suite was structurally blind was supplied to this lane by the hub and by its own agent brief, repeated confidently in both, and is recorded as refused in 11.43 itself. What survived is the ambiguity, now fixed upstream: three list shapes are documented, and a new bespoke shape MUST carry its reason in its own section 6 row -- with no reason it is a defect, with one it is a decision. Our filing is docs/2026-09-09-cr-s-bounded-list-consistency.md at 4b3b495; it is registered upstream as CR-T, since CR-S was already section 11.42's.

title: The I/O decode rule is applied on the read path and contradicted on the write path
detail: Fixed. The write arm decodes io_reg(a | 1) as the read arm does. The hardware question was settled from oracle-old's own decoder before dispatch (one discard expression at eight sites, four reads and four writes, parsed per mapping not per direction) and re-derived firsthand by the implementing agent. Its reframing is better than the finding: docs/2026-08-02-k4-openbus-design.md:178 already specified this decode direction-unqualified, so H31 was an INCOMPLETE LANDING of K4-4 rather than a modelling disagreement. The old covering test writes the ODD address and reads the even one, so it exercises the read mirror only and passed in the same run that showed the new test red. No frozen artifact moved, established by measurement: the only behaviour changed is an even-address BYTE write, word writes are unaffected because the low byte is written second, and no corpus ROM issues one.

title: The request side of the wire has a machine-readable contract and no differential against it
detail: Fixed by tests/request_bounds.rs, a differential that PARSES every numeric bound out of the vendored bus-protocol.schema.json at test time and sends one step outside each end; no bound is written down anywhere in the test. Six gates: the differential, a two-ended in-bounds anti-vacuity control, a coverage ledger requiring baselines-union-uncovered to equal the derived bounded set in both directions, an enumerable-surface report, an anti-rot check on the one registered divergence, and a hard-wired witness that the walk reads the document. MEASURED: 58 declared bound sites over the 32 advertised methods that carry any request bound; 41 sites covered, 17 declared UNCOVERED (the six object methods, which need a loaded act); 70 probes, all refused -32602 BY NAME, 0 accepted, 0 unmeasured. Full crate suite 609 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored. THE FINDING'S NUMBERS WERE ALL WRONG in the direction that mattered: not 57 bounds but 60 sites (58 on advertised methods), and not 62 handlers re-implementing bounds but 32 -- the other 30 advertised methods declare no request bound at all, so the surface was half the size reported. More importantly the premise was wrong: no handler anywhere the differential can reach defaults an out-of-bounds value instead of refusing it. emulator/step was the exception, not the sample. TWO NEW FINDINGS from running it. (1) F-Z80READ-LEN0-UNSERVEABLE: z80_read's fragment declares len minimum 0 -- alone among every len on the surface -- so len:0 is a request the contract PERMITS; the server answers bytes "0x"; result.bytes is $defs/hex whose pattern ^0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+$ requires at least one digit. No conformant reply exists, the server may not refuse it and cannot answer it. Nothing in the tree had ever sent it. BLOCKED as a fix (both remedies are the contract owner's and this parcel is hermetic); registered in KNOWN_UNSERVEABLE with anti-rot, and a mutation proved that widening the hex pattern to ^0x[0-9A-Fa-f]*$ is sufficient. (2) A false green inside the differential itself, caught only by its own in-bounds control: a write_memory baseline that paired disp with addr was refused -32602 naming disp -- for the param's COMPANY, not its VALUE -- so the out-of-bounds probe read as enforcement without ever reaching the bound. The by-name rule is necessary and not sufficient. Every gate proven red-first with the mutation quoted from disk and restored from a committed baseline: removing step's count floor reproduces the founding defect (ACCEPTED x2); stripping the field name out of hex::parse_count turns 14+ probes UNNAMED; tightening sprites.limit to 2 reddens the control alone while the differential stays green; adding a bound to an unruled fragment reddens three gates; widening $defs/hex reddens the anti-rot. Left open and enumerable: the six object methods (F-OBJ-BOUNDS-UNPROBED, 17 sites), and two ceilings the max control does not send -- press.frames 1000 (F-PRESS-CEILING-UNEXERCISED, the harness's one-frame budget legitimately refuses it) and wait_for_break.timeoutMs 300000 (F-WAITBREAK-CEILING-UNEXERCISED, reasoned not measured, since measuring costs five minutes). The finding's catch_unwind clause is true and deliberate: catch_unwind appears in no shipping crate, which oracle-core/src/z80/mod.rs argues for explicitly -- containment is structural refusal, not a wrapper at the handler boundary. Not treated as a defect here.

title: A per-line scroll value is fetched once per pixel, 320 times more often than it can change
detail: Fixed. plane_sample and plane_pixel now take the line's h-scroll as a parameter; the per-line hoist lives in LineCtx (was ASlotCtx), built once in resolve_line_masked and pixel_attribution_masked. The finding's own prescription was half a fix: it said the hoisted copy 'already sits in ASlotCtx three lines away', which is true for plane A only -- plane B is sampled on the same dots and had no hoisted copy at all, so reusing the existing field would have left half the per-dot fetches in place. The struct was renamed because a struct called ASlotCtx carrying b_hscroll would be a lie. Measured in the shipped binary by objdump: Vdp::plane_sample 201 -> 140 instructions. Picture parity is the whole acceptance test and it holds byte-for-byte -- all 6 golden_frames pins unchanged (incl. scene 4 hscroll_modes, this finding's own subject), plus a 600-frame real-ROM differential over fixtures/aeon/s4.debug.bin, 129,024,000 raw RGB bytes cmp-identical.

title: One hardware integer division per plane per dot, from a Vec::len() used as a modulus
detail: Fixed. Vdp::vsram_word wrapped with (idx * 2) % self.vsram().len(); len() on a Vec is a runtime value, so that was a real div, reached once per plane per dot through plane_vscroll. It now wraps by the constant VSRAM_SIZE -- the same authority Vdp::data_read already uses for its own VSRAM reads and the only length Vdp::new ever allocates -- with a debug_assert_eq! stating that assumption at the point it is made. Located by search, not by the filing, which recorded no line. Confirmed in the shipped binary by objdump: Vdp::plane_vscroll carried 4 div instructions before and 0 after, and the whole binary went 80 -> 76. In the render path the modulus never actually fired (H40's widest VSRAM index is 39, byte 78 of 80) -- nothing had told the compiler that. Same parity evidence as H12: 6 golden pins unchanged and a 129 MB byte-identical real-ROM framebuffer differential.

title: The Breakpoints delete button was undrawable and read as an unticked tick-box
detail: Packet finding 1 (UXb F-UXB-8). The label was U+2715, which no face in egui's bundled set carries, so it drew as the replacement box 36px right of a real tick-box; it deleted on the first click with no tooltip, confirmation or undo, and a seat lost a breakpoint to it while trying to re-enable one. Fixed as a WORD (ui::REMOVE_LABEL) plus a two-press confirm keyed on the server's handle, not a bundled font: a font fixes the drawing and leaves UX2 standing. Confirmation rather than undo because re-adding yields a new handle with hits reset, and this surface never resets a count. Durable half: screen::tests::every_string_literal_the_player_can_show_is_drawable, derived from main.rs's own mod declarations and a literal lexer, asking BOTH font families. Red-first on the pristine tree at 5 undrawable literals over 1792 lexed across 27 modules.

title: The ROM browser's `up` button was also a hollow box, and the obvious repair was too
detail: NOT a packet finding: found by UX1's new glyph gate on its first run, reported by nobody, because a box beside the word `up` reads as an ornament. U+2191 is drawable in the MONOSPACE family and not in the proportional one, and that button is proportional - which is why the gate asks about both rather than guessing a literal's call site. The obvious substitute U+25B2 is ALSO a box in the proportional family on a build where U+25B6 two buttons away draws fine: this font set's geometric shapes are patchy, not present. Measured, not assumed; the label is now the word.

title: One square meant disable in one tab and delete forever in the next
detail: Packet finding 2 (UXb F-UXB-13). In Watchpoints the square was the FIRST control in a row with no tick-box at all; in Breakpoints it was the second, after a real one. Closed by UX1's fix and not by a font, which is the reason UX1 chose a word: this survives any glyph repair. Both tabs now say `remove` and take the same two presses.

title: The Memory panel opened already refusing its own default, and one box had two behaviours
detail: Packet finding 4, convergence C-1. First click, nothing typed: 0xFFFF0000 and REFUSED -32004 beneath it, with ui.rs's hint advertising the same refused value. We documented this hazard in bus-protocol.schema.json's rawAddr note (signed 'found by hitting it') and then shipped it as the default. BOTH halves fixed: memory::DEFAULT_BASE = 0x00FF0000 feeds the box, the page base and the hint from one constant; and the numeric path now masks with oracle_core::symbols::BUS_ADDR_MASK exactly as the symbol path always has, carrying the listing spelling so the panel NAMES BOTH NUMBERS on screen. Bus space only. The schema note's rule is about a client that cannot read an explanation; loudness is what it protects, and a sentence achieves it here where a round trip achieves it on the wire.

title: The README did not know the debug window exists, or say where a ROM comes from
detail: Packet finding 7. grep -c oracle-player README.md was 0; Layout said 'Four crates' and the workspace has FIVE members (crates/ holds six directories, one deliberately excluded - so 'six' would have been a new wrong number, and the brief's six was corrected against the tree). Added oracle-player as the debug window, labelled oracle-frontend the game window, explained the excluded spike, added a section on the two windows being two separate machines (packet finding 3 / C-3, documentation half only), and a 'Where a ROM comes from' section - whose answer is better than the brief's: this repo SHIPS a committed bootable ROM at fixtures/aeon/s4.debug.bin. Run recipes now name real paths and add oracle-player with --rom, which is a flag there and not positional. Durable half: crates/oracle-player/tests/readme_layout_matches_the_workspace.rs checks the list both ways, accounts for every crates/ directory, requires an excluded one to be named, and makes any stated '<n> crates' self-checking. Red-first under four mutations.

title: WORK_RAM_LO is two different numbers under one name, and only one copy carries the derivation
detail: NOT a documentation fix, and the packet was right to flag that. Decided from source, not from either comment: oracle-core's bus decodes work RAM as 0xE0_0000..=0xFF_FFFF and folds the index with addr & (RAM_SIZE-1) at bus.rs:1048 (read) and :1170 (write) -- one 64 KiB chip, 128 mirrors -- so $E00000 is the DECODE and $FF0000 is merely the mirror the listing's FFFFxxxx symbols spell. oracle-aether's copy was right; oracle-replay's was wrong and widened to match. Live defect closed: stack_in_work_ram returned None for an A7 in any lower mirror, so decode_trap (runner.rs:760) booked a perfectly readable frame as StackNotInWorkRam. ram_u8/ram_u32 already folded correctly, so the range check was the only thing disagreeing with the hardware. The hazard runs BOTH ways -- unifying onto the narrow spelling would silently shrink the Aether server's RAM window -- which is why it is gated rather than tidied. GATED: the_work_ram_window_covers_every_mirror_the_bus_decodes, written before the fix and red on committed code (left: None, right: Some(0x00E00000)); it asserts the two spellings of one byte agree, so the narrowing unification goes red. oracle-replay 76 + 13 passed / 0 failed.

title: spawn::Mode's doc states an invariant the frontend's own F5 swap violates
detail: CODE fixed, not the doc weakened. Correction to the packet: it said 'the only disarm site is the explicit toggle'; there were TWO (main.rs's ToggleSpawnMode key and drain.rs's bus-driven listing replacement) and the missing third was the pending_rom swap block, which re-read the listing, re-pointed the bus and re-armed every symbol watch -- all for the D7 stale-address reason -- and walked past spawn_mode. So F5 left the mode armed holding the OUTGOING listing's archetype NAMES, which object_spawn re-resolves at call time: the click succeeds at a different address (92.6% of shared s4.lst/s4.debug.lst symbols name a different one). The drain could not have covered it and the engine says so: host.rs:801. Disarm added beside the watch re-arm; silent when never armed. A plain reset (Tab/F1) deliberately does NOT disarm -- it keeps the cartridge -- so the old doc was wrong on that half too. The doc now carries the exhaustive three-row table of listing-replacing sites and says the better shape (derive armed-ness from the listing generation) is not built and why. GATED: the_rom_swap_disarms_spawn_mode_so_a_click_cannot_land_on_a_stale_address, source-asserted on the_env_override_is_never_written_back_to_the_config's precedent; red-first with the fix removed from disk (failed on the intended assertion), restored, green. NEEDS THE OWNER'S EYE: the runtime half is unconfirmed by construction -- arm spawn mode, press F5, check the badge retracts.

title: The panel count: a correction applied to two files out of four
detail: WIDER THAN BOOKED, and the correction is the finding. The packet had nav.rs and screen.rs as already-correct at 'four of the eight'. They were not: Tab now has ELEVEN variants and initial_dock builds four leaves ([Screen,Planes], [Pacing,Spawn,Effects], [Registers,Memory,Objects], [Breakpoints,Watchpoints,Profiler]), so the standing figures are four run / seven hidden and ALL FOUR files were stale -- two at 'six of eight' and two at 'four of eight', the repo asserting two wrong numbers rather than one right and one wrong. Counted from Tab::ALL and the split_* calls, not from the packet. Sharpest instance: the doc comment on the very test praised for deriving rather than restating was ITSELF part of the second drift -- it enumerated the leaves and concluded 'four bodies run and four do not', while the assertions below it never said that and never went wrong. A derivation in the assertions and a restatement in the prose above them are not the same artifact. GATED: nav::tests::panel_counts_in_prose_match_the_enum pins the four sentences to Tab::ALL and the leaf count rather than to each other, compares whitespace-flattened text (these sentences rewrap and are spelled //!, /// and //), and carries an anti-vacuity control on the number-word table. Red-first: grew Tab::ALL to 12 and it failed naming all four files; ui.rs restored from the committed baseline. oracle-player 394 passed / 0 failed.

title: The SRAM field doc denies a currency it is in
detail: READING, not gated. Said SRAM is 'NOT in export_state (that go-live is S3)'. S3 shipped: export_state writes the SRAM tail region and EXPORT_SRAM_LEN's own doc says 'Added at the SRAM go-live slice (S3), bumping the version to 2'. export_state_hash is the determinism gate's currency, so a reader asking 'can an SRAM write move the gate?' got the wrong answer. The state_hash half was and stays correct. Confirmed the packet's observation that the neighbouring fields (sram_dirty, sram_used) make the same-shaped claim and ARE right -- which is why this one was never re-read. TWO MORE COPIES found and fixed beside the parcel (bus.rs's sram field, and the sram_dirty accessors booked as landing 'in S2' while sitting a few lines below) -- see 4cb45e7.

title: Three comments say the Z80 'steps zero instructions'
detail: READING, not gated. FOUR sites, not three (the packet's line numbers had drifted): system.rs:259, system.rs:1125 at the top of the production run loop, system.rs's catch_up_z80 doc ('Z80::step is never reached'), and bus.rs:832. The gate is live, export_state region 4 is live, and z80_executes_in_the_run_loop_when_released drives real instructions through it. The packet's 'nuance kept' was the key to doing this correctly: the accurate version is FIXTURE-SCOPED and was sitting in the same sentences -- no committed ROM fixture releases the Z80, so the corpus is unaffected and every frozen currency stays byte-identical. Rewritten to say that instead of the absolute. z80/mod.rs:8 was LEFT ALONE on purpose: it already scopes the claim correctly ('every committed fixture leaves the Z80 in reset'), and 'fixing' a true comment is the trap this class invites.

title: A seven-step staircase of 'never reaches decode' claims, all superseded
detail: READING, not gated. Seven arms of the 0xE shift/rotate cascade each froze a note of the form 'only ASL/.../ROXL files are loaded this commit, so no other 0xE op reaches decode'. All eight ops exist and the corpus loads all eight. Confirming the packet's 'even the last step is one behind': it is ROXL's note that still calls ROXR 'S7, not loaded', while ROXR's own arm already carries the corrected 'All eight shift/rotate ops are now loaded' -- the correction written in the last place and never propagated backwards, the same shape as H18 and H19. Nothing was broken; the hazard is a future edit made on a false disjointness premise, which is why reassurance-of-unreachability rates high. Replaced with one standing note at the top of the cascade telling the next author not to write that sentence again.

title: render_scanline documented as 'not wired into System::run'
detail: READING, not gated -- though the corrected fact does have a standing test. It is called from system.rs:1236 on every active line, and system.rs's scanline_wiring_evolves_the_sprite_masking_carry_during_a_run has been asserting 'render_scanline committed the dot-overflow carry on line 223 during the run' in the other file the whole time. The currency parenthetical ('so the export golden is untouched') is the dangerous half: it invites a reader to treat the method as currency-free and edit it accordingly. That test was not added here and would not fail if the comment were reverted.

title: The symbol-file acceptance policy is written out FOUR times; three survive retirement
detail: READING, not gated -- and it cannot be gated, which is the finding. policy.rs said 'This is the third copy of that table ... It is the immediately-following slice, not a follow-up ticket.' It is the fourth (oracle-player/src/symbols.rs landed), the extraction never happened, and the two line-number citations had drifted ~6,100 lines. Positional citations replaced with symbol names -- citing a moving file by position is its own small lesson. Recorded why no test can assert the four agree: oracle-replay depends on oracle-core alone, so no crate sees the replay copy and any other at once. The four-arm table includes the fail-open guard (Indeterminate + not intact -> refuse), so a drift on that arm accepts a listing for a different ROM and every annotation is confidently wrong. They agree TODAY -- checked by reading all four, not by a gate. Fix shape is extraction into oracle-core::symbols, where a compile-time agreement becomes possible at all. NOT DONE HERE.

title: Two copies of the completed-frame reader; only one is tested, and the untested one answers the wire
detail: ALREADY CLOSED when this parcel opened, by H25's unification (2c04414, on main): H9 and H25 are one subject and the fix for the four-copy finding closed the two-copy one. Verified rather than assumed: the selection now lives once in ScanlineCapture::completed_frame with each consumer keeping only its own packing loop, and blit_capture / store_from_capture both call it. H25's claim that one mutation to the shared width rule turns the consumers red was then TESTED by mutating widths[height-1] -> widths[0] (the ragged-frame rule) and running all four consumer crates with --no-fail-fast; see the parcel report for which targets went red. No further change made and none needed.

title: rings.rs's bounds guard checks 4 of 9 listing offsets, and the check it does perform overflows in release
detail: All nine offsets now live in one table (Layout::offsets) that check() walks with checked_add, so checking them and using them cannot come apart; the three products the module derives from the same unchecked equates are checked_mul'd too, since a wrapped product is a short read into the same index expressions. Gate: the_bounds_check_covers_every_offset_field_the_layout_declares reads the module's own source and fails for an offset field nobody thought to list. TWO CORRECTIONS to the finding as booked: (a) the damage is an index PANIC, not a byte written into the next ring -- Rust bounds-checks slice indexing in every profile; (b) a '-1'-spelled equate does NOT reach the overflow, since a 32-bit assembler spells it $FFFFFFFF and that does not overflow u64. The wrap needs a 16-hex-digit equate and the parser's own doc records 8 as the widest ever seen, so the incomplete-coverage half is the live one. The wrap was still demonstrated: with the old arithmetic restored, --release returned Ok for a u64::MAX offset (the confident pass) while dev panicked with 'attempt to add with overflow'.

title: Drained::symbols is published and has ZERO consumers — the player copied the frontend's signal but not its repair
detail: Repair wired, not signal removed -- but the obvious wiring was wrong twice and that is the finding. Drained::symbols is a repair RECEIPT (symbols_changed || rom_changed), so it is true after emulator/reset, which KEEPS the listing; and own.symbols_changed is raised by this window's OWN preview, because screen_pick takes a checkpoint per arm and checkpoint_restore bumps symbols_generation unconditionally -- so keyed on the union, arming spawn mode raised the signal that retracted it on the next drain. Both caught by a control written before the gate (a_quiet_iteration_leaves_the_object_mode_armed). Published fact is now Drained::listing_replaced_by_a_client = report.symbols_changed alone. The sentence is one const (spawn::DISARMED_BY_LISTING_CHANGE) quoted by both windows. Ring mode deliberately survives a listing change: it reads its bounds at click time. RESIDUAL GAP TAGGED: a listing this window replaces itself does not retract the mode; the remedy is H21's identity-based arming, which is a change to the shared spawn::Mode and out of this parcel's scope.

title: Two identical serialized enums for "which VDP memory", 1,600 lines apart in one module
detail: Target deleted, VdpTarget survives with the merged doc: one type, three consumers (the data-port decode, VdpWrite, DmaRecord). VdpTarget kept because it was already the spelling at four sites outside the module against Target's one. Merge is byte-identical on the wire and provably so: bincode encodes an enum as its variant index and both lists were Vram, Cram, Vsram in that order, so no save-state or frame_report expectation moved. No gate added, deliberately -- divergence is now unrepresentable rather than checked, and a gate asserting two types agree is the comment this parcel exists to remove. NOTE for the owner: several dated docs/ recon files quote Target::Vram; left alone as dated records of the tree as it was, not rewritten.

title: Two mutually-exclusive click modes kept as two bools, and the clearing happens before the fallible arm
detail: arm_spawn now runs both fallible steps first and returns on either refusal having moved nothing but self.last; the exclusion is part of the commit rather than part of the attempt, so there is no window in which one mode is off and the other is not yet on. Both refusal arms driven with a different fixture each (-32012 no listing, -32013 a listing naming no ObjDef_), and each proved independently red under the restored ordering. DESIGN CALL on the brief's 'a type that cannot represent both-at-once': NOT taken, with reason. Object armed-ness lives inside oracle_frontend::spawn::Mode, a type shared with the frontend, so an enum here would not remove the second bool -- Mode::is_armed() would remain independently readable and the enum would be a THIRD source of truth for one fact, which is this parcel's own defect class. The unrepresentable version needs armed-ness moved out of spawn::Mode; flagged for the owner.
